questions.q: Let& $A = \left\{\theta \in \left(0, 2\pi\right): \dfrac{1 + 2isin\theta}{1 - isin\theta}ispurelyimaginary\right\}$~Then the sum of the elements is in~$A$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$z = \dfrac{1 + 2isin\theta}{1 - isin\theta}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{1 + 2isin\theta}{1 - isin\theta} \times \dfrac{1 + isin\theta}{1 + isin\theta}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta + 3isin\theta}{1 + \sin^{2}\theta}$

$⇒ z = \left(\dfrac{1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta}{1 + \sin^{2}\theta}\right) + i \left(\dfrac{3sin\theta}{1 + \sin^{2}\theta}\right)

Since,~$z$~is a purely imaginary number, so real part must be zero, hence

\dfrac{1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta}{1 + \sin^{2}\theta} =$0$

$⇒ 1 - 2\sin^{2}$\theta =$0$

$⇒ cos2$\theta =$0$

$⇒ $\theta = \dfrac{π}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}, for~\theta \in \left($0, $2\pi\right)

$∴$Sum of all values~$= $\dfrac{16\pi}{4} ==4\pi$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{z \in C: \left|z - 1\right| = 1and\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - i\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) = 2\sqrt{2}\right\}$. Let ${z}_{1}, {z}_{2} \in S$ be such that \left|{z}_{1}\right| = \mathop\max_{z \in s}\left|z\right|$ and \left|{z}_{2}\right| = \mathop\min_{z \in s}\left|z\right|$. Then \left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2$ equals:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|z - 1\right| = 1$

Now, let $z = x + iy$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)2 + y^{2} = 1 . . . \left($i\right)$

And

\$left(\sqrt{2} -1\right)\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - i\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2} -1\right)\left(2x\right) - i \left($2iy\right) = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2} -$1\right)x + y = $\sqrt{2} . . . \left($ii\right)$

Solving \left(i\$right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)2 + \$left[\sqrt{2} - \left(\sqrt{2} -$1\right)x\right]2 = 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 1 - 2x + 2 + \$left(\sqrt{2} -$1\right)2x^{2} - $2\sqrt{2} \left(\sqrt{2} -$1\right)x = 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 1 - 2x + 2 + \left(2 + 1 - $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x^{2} - 4x + $2\sqrt{2}$x = 1$

$⇒ x^{2} - 2x + 2 + 3x^{2} - $2x^{2}\sqrt{2} -$4x + $2\sqrt{2}$x = 0$

$⇒ 4x^{2} - $2x^{2}\sqrt{2} -$6x + $2\sqrt{2}$x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x^{2} + \left(- 6 + $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x^{2} + \left(- 4 + $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x - 2x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x\left(x - 1\right) - 2 \left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(\left(4 - $2\sqrt{2}\right)$x - 2\right) = 0$

Either $x = 1$ or $x = $\dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{2}} . . . \left(iii\right)$

On solving \left(ii\right)\text{and} \left($iii\right)$ we get

For $x = 1 ⇒ y = 1 ⇒ {z}_{2} = 1 + i$ and for $x = \dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{2}}⇒ y = \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}⇒ {z}_{1} = \left($1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{i}{2}$

$⇒ \left|$\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2 = \left|\$left(\dfrac{1}{2} +1\right)\sqrt{2} +i - \left($1 + i\right)\right|2$

$⇒ \left|$\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2 = \left|$1 + \sqrt{2} +i - \left($1 + i\right)\right|2$

$⇒ \left|$\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2 = \left(\sqrt{2}\right)$2$

$⇒ \left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|$2 = 2$

$

questions.q: Let $z \in C$ be such that \left|z\right| < 1 .$ If $\omega = \dfrac{5 + 3z}{5\left(1 - z\right)},$ then:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& \left|z\right| < 1$~and~$\omega = \dfrac{5 + 3z}{5\left(1 - z\right)}$

$⇒ 5\omega\left(1 - z\right) = 5 + 3z$

$⇒ 5\omega - 5\omegaz = 5 + 3z$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{5\omega - 5}{3 + 5\omega}$

Using the given condition~\left|z\right| = 5\left|\dfrac{\omega - 1}{3 + 5\omega}\right| < 1$


$⇒ 5\left|\omega - 1\right| < \left|3 + 5\omega\right|$

$⇒ 5\left|\omega - 1\right| < 5\left|\omega + \dfrac{3}{5}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\omega - 1\right| < \left|\omega - \left(- \dfrac{3}{5}\right)\right|$

We know that the locus of a complex number~${z}_{1}$~satisfying \left|{z}_{1} - a\right| = \left|{z}_{2} - b\right|$~is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points~$a$~and~$b .$

Hence, the~locus of the point~$\omega$~satisfying~\left|\omega - 1\right| = \left|\omega - \left(- \dfrac{3}{5}\right)\right|$~is the line~$x = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{3}{5}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

Hence, $Re\left(\omega\right) > \dfrac{1}{5}$

$⇒ 5Re\left(\omega\right) > 1 .$

questions.q: Let $A = \left\{z \in C: \left|\dfrac{z + 1}{z - 1}\right| < 1\right\}$~and $B = \left\{z \in C: arg\left(\dfrac{z - 1}{z + 1}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right\}$.~Then $A ∩ B$& is
options: a portion of a circle centred at&  \left(0, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$& that lies in the second and third quadrants only$
a portion of a circle centred at&  \left(0, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$& that lies in the second quadrant only$
a portion of a circle of radius& $\dfrac{2}{3}$& that lies in the third quadrant only
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Set& $A$~is~\left\{z \in C: \left|\dfrac{z + 1}{z - 1}\right| < 1\right\}$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\overset{¯}{z} + 1}{\overset{¯}{z} - 1}\right| < 1$

$⇒ \left|\overset{¯}{z} + 1\right| < \left|\overset{¯}{z} - 1\right|$

$⇒ \left(x + 1\right)2 + y^{2} < \left(x - 1\right)2 + y^{2}$

$⇒ x < 0$

Set~$B$~is~\left\{z \in C: arg\left(\dfrac{z - 1}{z + 1}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right\}$

$⇒ arg\left(\dfrac{z - 1}{z + 1}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x - 1}\right) - \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x + 1}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + \dfrac{2y}{3} - 1 = 0$

$⇒$~ Centre~ \left(0, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

Hence,~$A ∩ B$~will represent a portion of a circle centred at~ \left(0, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$& that lies in the second quadrant only

questions.q: If for& $z = \alpha + i\beta, \left|z + 2\right| = z + 4 ( 1 + i ) ,$~then~$\alpha + \beta$~and~$\alpha\beta$& are the roots of the equation&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$z = \alpha + i\beta \text{ and } \left|z + 2\right| = z + 4 \left($1 + i\right)$

Now putting the value of~$z = $\alpha ++i\beta$~in~ \left|$z + 2\right| = z + 4 \left($1 + i\right)$~we get,

\left|z + 2\right| = z + 4 \left($1 + i\right)$

$⇒ $\sqrt{ \left(\alpha +$2\right)2 + {β}^{2}}=\left(\alpha +$4\right) + $i\left(\beta +$4\right)$

Now on comparing real and imaginary part, we get

\sqrt{( \alpha + 2{)}^{2} + {β}^{2}} = \alpha +$4 . . . ( i )$~and \beta +$4 = 0 ⇒ $\beta = -$4 . . . ( ii )$

Now solving,

\sqrt{( \alpha + 2{)}^{2} + 16} = \alpha +$4$

$⇒ {α}^{2} + $4\alpha +$20 = {α}^{2} + $8\alpha +$16$

$⇒ $\alpha =$1$

So,~\alpha + \beta = -$3, $\alpha\beta = -$4$

We know that quadratic equation is given by,

$x^{2} - \left(\text{sum of roots}\right)$x + \left(\text{product of roots}\right) =$0$

So, equation with roots~$- 3$~and~$- 4$~will be,

$x^{2} + 7x + 12 = 0

$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C} - { i, 2i } : \dfrac{z^{2} + 8iz - 15}{z^{2} - 3iz - 2} \in \mathbb{R}\right\}$. $\alpha - \dfrac{13}{11}i \in S, \alpha \in \mathbb{R} - { 0 }$, then $242{α}^{2}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Put& $z = x + iy$~in the given expression and equate the imaginary part to zero.

$⇒ \dfrac{z^{2} + 8iz - 15}{z^{2} - 3iz - 2} = \dfrac{\left(x + iy\right)2 + 8i\left(x + iy\right) - 15}{\left(x + iy\right)2 - 3i\left(x + iy\right) - 2}$

$= \dfrac{x^{2} - y^{2} - 8y - 15 + i\left(2xy + 8x\right)}{x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2 + i\left(2xy - 3x\right)}$

$= \dfrac{x^{2} - y^{2} - 8y - 15 + i\left(2xy + 8x\right)}{x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2 + i \left($2xy - 3x\right)} $\times \left($x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2 - i \left(2xy - 3x\right)\right)\left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2 - i \left($2xy - 3x\right)\right)$

$= \dfrac{\left(x^{2} - y^{2} - 8y - 15\right)\left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2\right) + \left(2xy + 8x\right)\left(2xy - 3x\right) + i\left(2xy + 8x\right)\left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2\right) - i\left(2xy - 3x\right)\left(x^{2} - y^{2} - 8y - 15\right)}{\left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2\right)2 - \left(2xy - 3x\right)2}$

But~Im\left(\dfrac{z^{2} + 8iz - 15}{z^{2} - 3iz - 2}\right) =$0$,

$⇒ - \left($x^{2} - y^{2} - 8y - 15\right)\left(2xy - 3x\right) + \left(2xy + 8x\right)\left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 3y - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x^{2} - y^{2}\$right)\left($2xy + 8x - 2xy + 3x\right) + \left($8y + 15\$right)\left($2xy - 3x\right) + \left($2xy + 8x\right)\left(3y - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ 11x^{3} - 11xy^{2} + 16xy^{2} - 24xy + 30xy - 45x + 6xy^{2} - 4xy + 24xy - 16x = 0$

$⇒ 11x^{3} + 11xy^{2} + 26xy - 61x = 0$

$⇒ 11x^{2} + 11y^{2} + 26y - 61 = 0$

$∵ \alpha \ne0$

So, put~$y = - $\dfrac{13}{11},~$x = \alpha$
$11{α}^{2} + 11 \cdot $\dfrac{132}{112} -$26 \cdot $\dfrac{13}{11} -$61 = 0$
$⇒ 121{α}^{2} = 840$

$⇒ 242{α}^{2} = 1680$

Hence this is the required answer.

$

questions.q: If $f ( x )$ and $g ( x )$ are two polynomials such that the polynomial $P ( x ) = f \left(x^{3}\right) + xg  \left($x^{3}\right)$ is divisible~by $x^{2} + x + 1$, then $P ( 1 )$ is equal to ___ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let $A=\{z \in C:|z-2-i|=3\}$, $B=\{z \in C: \operatorname{Re}(z-i z)=2\}$ and $S=A \cap B$. Then $\sum_{z \in S}|z|^2$ is equal to ________ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $z=x+i y$
$\begin{aligned}
& A:|z-2-i|=3 \\ & |(x-2)+(y-1) i|=3 \\ & (x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=9 ....(1)\\ & B=\operatorname{Re}(z-i z)=2 \\ & \operatorname{Re}((x+y)+i(y-x))=2 \\ & x+y=2....(2)
\end{aligned} .$
On solving (1) and (2) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& x=\frac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}, y=\frac{1 \mp \sqrt{17}}{2} \\ & \sum_{z \in \mathrm{~s}}|z|^2=\frac{1}{4}[2 \times 26+2 \times 18] \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{88}{4}=22
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let& $S = \left\{z \in C: \left|z - 2\right| \le 1, z\left(1 + i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(1 - i\right) \le 2\right\}$. Let \left|z - 4i\right|$~attains minimum and maximum values, respectively, at ${z}_{1} \in S$~and ${z}_{2} \in S$.~If $5\left(\left|{z}_{1}\right|2 + \left|{z}_{2}\right|2\right) = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{5}$, where $\alpha$~and $\beta$~are integers, then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& \left|z - 2\right| \le 1$

\left(x - 2\right)2 + y^{2} \le 1 ⋯ \left(i\right)$~represents~interior region of~a circle with centre \left(2, 0\right)$~and radius~$1$

Now~$z\left(1 + i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(1 - i\right) \le 2$

Puting~$z = x + iy$, we get

\left(x + iy\right)\left(1 + i\right) + \left(x - iy\right)\left(1 - i\right) \le 2$

$⇒ x - y + i \left(x + y\right) + x - y - i \left($x + y\right) ≤ 2$

$∴ x - y ≤ 1 \ldots \left($i\right)$

Let~$A \left(1, 0\right)$~and~$B \left(2, 1\right)$~be the points on the line~$x - y = 1$~and the circle~ \left($x - 2\right)2 + y^{2} = 1$

\left|$z - 4i\right|$~represents the distance from~P\left($0, 4\right)$~to any point in the region~$S$

Here~$PA = \sqrt{17},PB = \sqrt{13}$~

So~$A \left(1, 0\right)$~is~the point representing~${z}_{2}$

Let~$D \left($2 + $cos\theta,$0 + $sin\theta\right)~be the point representing~${z}_{1}$

$∴ {m}_{CP} = $tan\theta = -$2$

cos\theta = - $\dfrac{1}{5},$sin\theta = $\dfrac{2}{5}$

$∴ D ≡ \left(2 - $\dfrac{1}{5}, \dfrac{2}{5}\right)

$⇒ {z}_{1} = \left(2 - $\dfrac{1}{5}\right) + \dfrac{2i}{5}

So~\left|{z}_{1}\right| = $\dfrac{25 - 4\sqrt{5}}{5}$& {z}_{2} = 1$

$∴ \left|{z}_{2}\right|2 = 1$

$∴ 5\left(\left|{z}_{1}\right|2 + \left|{z}_{2}\right|2\right) = 30 - $4\sqrt{5}

$∴ \alpha =30$

$\beta = -4$

Hence~$\alpha + \beta =26

$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ denotes the number of solutions of  \left|1 - i\right|x = {2}^{x}$ and $\beta = \left(\left|z\right|arg\left(z\right)\right)$, where $z = \dfrac{π}{4}\left(1 + i\right)4 \left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}{\sqrt{\pi} + i} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - i}{1 + \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}\right), $i = $\sqrt{- 1}, then the distance of the point \left(\alpha, \beta\right) from the line $4x - 3y = 7 is ______$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|1 - i\right|x = {2}^{x}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2}\right)x = {2}^{x}$

$⇒ x = 0$

Hence, the number of solutions will be one, so $\alpha = 1$

Now, solving

$z = \dfrac{π}{4}\left(1 + i\right)4 \left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}{\sqrt{\pi} + i} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - i}{1 + \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}\right)

$⇒ z = $\dfrac{π}{4}\left($1 + i\right)4\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - \pii - i - \sqrt{\pi}}{\pi + 1} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - i - \pii - \sqrt{\pi}}{1 + \pi}\right]

$⇒ z = $\dfrac{π}{4}\left(1 + i\right)4 \left[\dfrac{- 2\pii - 2i}{\pi + 1}\right]

$⇒ z = $\dfrac{\pii}{2} \left($1 + i\right)4$

$⇒ z = - \dfrac{\pii}{2}\left(1 + 4i + 6i^{2} + 4i^{3} + 1\right)$

$⇒ z = 2\pii$

So, arg\left($z\right) = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ $\beta = \left|$z\right|$arg \left(z\right) = $\dfrac{2\pi}{\dfrac{π}{2}} =$4$

Hence, the distance from \left(\alpha, \beta\right)≡ \left(1, 4\right)$ to $4x - 3y = 7$ will be \left|\dfrac{4 - 3 \times 4 - 7}{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}\right| = \dfrac{15}{5} =3$
